hook: No culinary school. No meat. Just *two mothers.*
dek: Chef Yesenia Ramdass built HAAM in Williamsburg, Brooklyn, on recipes from her mom and her mother-in-law. Vegan Dominican food you'd swear was chicken.

slides.label: The chef
slides.text: Chef *Yesenia Ramdass* grew up in a Dominican home in *Washington Heights*. No culinary school. "This is my *culinary school* right here," she says, pointing at her mural.

slides.label: Two mothers
slides.text: Her mother and her *Trinidadian mother-in-law* taught her to cook. Both are painted on HAAM's wall. *Healthy As A Motha* is an ode to them.

slides.label: Elsa Strong
slides.text: Hidden in the greenery: butterflies whose legs and antennas spell *Elsa Strong*, for her late mother. Our founder Danny's mother is named *Elsa*, too.

slides.label: The rise
slides.text: Pop-ups, a delivery kitchen in *Sunnyside*, a Smorgasburg hit. On *Nov. 15, 2023* she and her husband *Randy* opened on Union Ave. HAAM turns *3* this month.

slides.label: The team
slides.text: Yesenia runs the kitchen. *Randy* runs operations. You can feel how well they work together in *every plate* and in how the whole night moves.

slides.label: The room
slides.text: *Pico Duarte* on one wall, *Mount Aripo* on the other, banana leaves with real plátanos. "Two islands, two cultures, two mothers, but *one house, one love*."

slides.label: The order
slides.text: *Yuh Motha's Mofongo* in curried cream and the *Crispy Cou Cou* with scotch bonnet honey glazed steak. You would never guess it's *not chicken*.

slides.label: The Den's take
slides.text: *Dominican vibes*, real hospitality and no compromise on flavor. Orlando grew up a few blocks from her. It felt like *home*. Te pasaste.

yt_title: Vegan Dominican Food in Brooklyn: No Culinary School, No Meat
caption_instagram:
Vegan Dominican food in Brooklyn, built by two mothers 🌱🇩🇴🇹🇹

Chef Yesenia Ramdass (@yeseniaramdass) never went to culinary school. Her teachers were her mom and her Trinidadian mother-in-law, and both are painted on the wall at @healthyasamotha in Williamsburg. Look closer: the butterflies in the greenery spell out "Elsa Strong" for her mom. (Our founder's mother is named Elsa, too. That one hit home.)

She runs the kitchen, her husband Randy (@randyramdass) runs operations (a true @house_of_ramdass), and on November 15 HAAM turns 3.

Order: Yuh Motha's Mofongo and the Crispy Cou Cou with Glazed Steak. Every plate is plant-based, and we still swear that mofongo was chicken.
📍 234 Union Ave, Williamsburg, Brooklyn

Who taught you to cook? 👇 Save this for your next Brooklyn night, and send it to the friend who says vegan food can't taste like home.

caption_linkedin:
She never went to culinary school. She built a restaurant on what two mothers taught her.

Chef Yesenia Ramdass grew up in Washington Heights, learned to cook from her mother and her Trinidadian mother-in-law, and turned that into HAAM (Healthy As A Motha), a plant-based Dominican and Trinidadian restaurant in Williamsburg. The path was not a straight line: years of pop-ups, a delivery kitchen in Sunnyside, a Smorgasburg stand, then a full restaurant that turns 3 this month.

What stood out when we sat with her on Thursday:

1. She built on what she knew. "This is my culinary school right here," she said, pointing at the mural of the two mothers.
2. She built it with her partner. She runs the kitchen, her husband Randy runs operations, and it shows in how the room runs.
3. She builds with women, in a kitchen industry where she is often the only female chef of color in the room.
4. She never traded culture for the concept. "Two islands, two cultures, two mothers, but one house, one love."

Which of the four matters most in your business?
